en: a. protected from a disease because of having had it before or having been vaccinated; not affected by something; not subject to something such as a law or tax; n. a person who is protected from a disease
ex: After the vaccination, she became immune to the virus.
接種疫苗後，她對這種病毒產生了免疫力。

en: n. a place where people have their hair cut or styled; a shop that provides beauty treatments; a gathering of artists and writers; a large room in a big house where guests are received
ex: She goes to the hair salon once a month.
她每個月去一次美髮沙龍。

en: vt. to make something as small as possible; to make something seem less important; to reduce the size of a window on a computer screen; vi. to become as small as possible
ex: We should minimize the risk of accidents.
我們應該把事故風險降到最低。

en: n. a man who owns a house, apartment or land and rents it to other people; the owner of a pub or hotel; a person who owns a lot of land
ex: The landlord raised the rent again this year.
房東今年又調漲了房租。

en: n. a lawyer, especially one who represents people in a court of law; (American) a lawyer; a person who is legally allowed to act for someone else
ex: The attorney represented the company in court.
律師在法庭上代表公司。

en: a. in a natural state and not yet processed; simple and not skillfully made; rude and offensive; n. oil that comes out of the ground and has not yet been treated
ex: The price of crude oil rose sharply this week.
本週原油價格大幅上漲。

en: a. relating to the government of a city or town; belonging to a city or town; (of a law) relating to a city
ex: The municipal government plans to build a new library.
市政府計畫興建一座新圖書館。

en: v. to pay back money that you have borrowed; to do something good for someone who has helped you; to do something in return for something done to you
ex: I will repay the loan within two years.
我會在兩年內還清貸款。

en: n. a large, important organization such as a university, hospital or bank; a custom or practice that has existed for a long time; the act of starting something; a place where people are cared for
ex: The bank is a financial institution with a long history.
這間銀行是歷史悠久的金融機構。

en: a. very unpleasant or bad; (of a person) unkind or cruel; (of a smell or taste) very unpleasant; dangerous or serious
ex: He has a nasty habit of interrupting people.
他有打斷別人說話的壞習慣。

en: a. very silly or unreasonable; making people laugh in a way that is not respectful; extremely foolish
ex: It is ridiculous to pay so much for a simple shirt.
為一件簡單的襯衫付這麼多錢太荒謬了。
ph: from the sublime to the ridiculous

en: n. a stick with burning material at one end used to give light; (British) an electric light that you hold in your hand; something that gives guidance or hope; vt. to set fire to something
ex: He used a torch to find his way in the dark cave.
他用手電筒在黑暗的洞穴裡找路。

en: n. a small lever that you press to fire a gun; an event that causes something to happen; something that makes someone remember something bad; vt. to cause something to start; to cause something to happen; vi. to cause something to start
ex: A loud noise triggered the car alarm.
一聲巨響觸發了汽車警報器。

en: vt. to mention something as an example or proof; to quote the words of someone; to officially praise someone; to order someone to appear in a court
ex: The writer cited several studies to support her argument.
作者引用了好幾項研究來支持她的論點。

en: n. a person who is not loyal to their country, friends or group; a person who gives secrets to an enemy
ex: He was branded a traitor after selling state secrets.
他出賣國家機密後被貼上叛徒的標籤。

en: n. a person who does not belong to a particular group or organization; a person who has no knowledge about a particular subject; a competitor who is not expected to win
ex: She felt like an outsider at the new school.
她在新學校裡覺得自己像個局外人。

en: a. showing or feeling strong emotions; very enthusiastic about something; having or showing strong sexual or romantic feelings; (of a person) easily becoming angry
ex: She is passionate about environmental protection.
她對環境保護充滿熱情。

en: n. a period of time between two events; a short break between parts of a play, concert or other event; the distance between two places or things; a break between two periods of work or study
ex: There will be a fifteen-minute interval after the first act.
第一幕後會有十五分鐘的中場休息。

en: a. showing great interest and excitement about something; very eager to do something; having or showing strong interest in something
ex: The students were enthusiastic about the school trip.
學生們對校外教學感到很興奮。

en: n. the way you think about or understand something; the ability to see, hear or notice something; a quick, intuitive understanding of something; the way something appears to you
ex: Our perception of time changes as we get older.
隨著年紀增長，我們對時間的感知會改變。

en: a. small and neatly arranged; closely and firmly packed; (of a style of writing) brief and clear; vt. to press something tightly together; n. a small case with a mirror that holds powder; a small car
ex: The apartment is compact but very comfortable.
這間公寓小巧但非常舒適。

en: a. connected with God or a religion and deserving great respect; very important and not to be questioned; (of a place or object) used in religious ceremonies; having a special value
ex: The temple is a sacred place for many pilgrims.
這座廟宇對許多朝聖者來說是神聖之地。

en: adv. as a result of what has just been mentioned; by that means; in that way
ex: He signed the contract and thereby became the new owner.
他簽了合約，因此成為新的所有人。

en: n. the first public appearance of a performer, a product or a show; the beginning of a career; the first time that something is shown or used; vi. to perform or appear in public for the first time; vt. to introduce a product for the first time
ex: The young singer made her debut at a concert hall.
那位年輕歌手在音樂廳初次登台。

en: n. a flat metal frame for cooking food over a fire; a restaurant that serves grilled food; a set of metal bars; vt. to cook food on a metal frame over a fire; to question someone for a long time; vi. to cook on a grill
ex: He grilled some steaks on the barbecue grill.
他在烤肉架上烤了幾塊牛排。

en: n. an idea or explanation of something that is based on a few known facts but has not yet been proved; a suggestion that is made as a starting point for an argument or research
ex: Scientists tested the hypothesis through experiments.
科學家透過實驗來檢驗這個假設。

en: n. a part of a legal document that states a condition or rule; a group of words that contains a subject and a verb and forms part of a sentence; a section of a treaty or contract
ex: The contract includes a clause about payment.
合約中有一條關於付款的條款。

en: vt. to pull something heavy with effort; to carry things in a truck or vehicle; vi. to pull something with a lot of effort; to change direction; n. the act of pulling something with effort; an amount of something gained; a distance over which something is carried
ex: They hauled the boat onto the beach.
他們把船拖上了海灘。

en: n. the place where someone or something is; the approximate position of someone or something; adv. in or near what place
ex: The police are trying to find out his whereabouts.
警方正在設法查明他的下落。

en: vt. to think that something is probably true; to accept something as true without proof; to take liberties with someone; vi. to be too confident or to act boldly
ex: I presume that you have already had dinner.
我猜你已經吃過晚餐了。

en: n. the act of making something longer or bigger; an additional part added to a building; an additional telephone line; extra time given to finish something; a. able to be extended
ex: I'd like to request an extension on the deadline.
我想申請延長截止日期。

en: n. a serious promise to do something; a formal promise, especially a religious one; vt. to promise very seriously that you will do something; vi. to make a serious promise
ex: They exchanged wedding vows in a church.
他們在教堂交換結婚誓言。

en: adv. not in or to any place; used to say that you cannot find or reach somewhere; n. a place that is far away or not important
ex: There was nowhere to sit in the crowded room.
擁擠的房間裡沒有地方可以坐。

en: n. a long thin straight stick or bar; a bar of metal or wood; a stick used for fishing; (old) a cane for punishing children
ex: He used a fishing rod to catch fish at the lake.
他用釣竿在湖邊釣魚。

en: n. a person who writes regular articles for a newspaper or magazine; a person who writes about a particular subject
ex: The columnist wrote an article about city politics.
專欄作家寫了一篇關於城市政治的文章。

en: vt. to make someone very sad; vi. to feel very sad, especially because someone has died; to feel sorrow
ex: The family grieved over the loss of their grandfather.
全家人為失去祖父而悲痛。

en: n. a mathematical statement showing that two amounts are equal; the process of making something equal; a situation in which several factors must be considered together; a chemical formula
ex: The teacher wrote an equation on the board.
老師在黑板上寫了一個方程式。

en: vt. to be more than a particular number or amount; to go beyond a limit; to be better than someone or something; vi. to be better than others
ex: The cost of the project exceeded the budget.
專案成本超出了預算。

en: vt. to change something from one form or use to another; to change money into another currency; to make someone change their beliefs or religion; vi. to change from one belief or religion to another; n. a person who has changed their religion or beliefs
ex: They converted the old barn into a house.
他們把舊穀倉改建成住宅。

en: n. the state of having many parts and being difficult to understand; something that is complicated; the number of factors involved in a situation
ex: The complexity of the problem made it hard to solve.
問題的複雜性使它很難解決。
